newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares hit new records, dlr struggles.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares hit new records, dlr struggles.

text.p: Leading European bourses rang up new record closes on Friday though they were knocked off the highs they made during the morning by a sharp slide on Wall Street.
The dollar also went into reverse after its early attempts to recoup some of the heavy losses it suffered against the yen on Thursday came to nought amid fears of intervention.
The Dow Jones industrial index of top U.S. shares was down around 40 points at the end of European trading following a sell off prompted by stronger-than-expected figures on U.S. housing starts.

Total starts were up 2.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.47 million in April after a revised 7.7 percent drop to 1.43 million in March, the U.S. government said. Analysts had forecast a rate of 1.43 million.
Traders were also wary ahead of the key meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank's interest rate setting forum on Tuesday.
The majority of economists believe the U.S. central bank will raise rates to forestall the threat of inflation.

London's FTSE 100 ended with a gain of just 12.7 points at 4,693.9, having hit a fresh intra-day high of 4,723.7 during the morning as stock shortages continued and amid position-closing ahead of the weekend. The close was its ninth closing high out of the last 11 sessions.
Prices were boosted from the outset by an overnight Dow record and with selected shares squeezed sharply higher by a shortage of stock in the market.

French stocks also rose to record close, the third in a row, which saw the blue-chip CAC-40 index end with a gain of 8.27 points, or 0.3 percent, at 2,784.28 after easing from its session and all-time high of 2,804.51 points hit during the morning.
The market was bolstered by gains in bond prices, Wall Street's gains overnight and a fresh Ipsos poll showing the conservatives leading in the upcoming parliamentary election.

The Ipsos poll for the magazine Le Point projected the ruling RPR-UDF coalition would win 323 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, up from 290 in a similar poll last week. It indicated the Socialists would trail with 266 seats.

In Frankfurt, the DAX index ended with a gain of 42.44 points, or 1.2 percent, at a new record of 3,604.55. Traders said the move was underpinned by Wall Street's overnight close and the dollar's foray above 1.70 marks.
But the DAX had closed before Wall Street opened and the DAX Ibis index of electronic trading ended up just 4.41 points at 3,569.26.

In currencies, the dollar ended a punishing week sharply weaker against the yen, leaving the market abuzz with speculation of intervention to sell yen just weeks after the talk was all of concerted buying.
Only last week, the dollar's persistent strength sparked fears of joint intervention to dampen it, plus a chorus of yen-positive comments from Japanese officials.

The market took heed. In just 15 days, the dollar has plunged almost 13 yen. "It's incredible that only a few weeks ago they were trying to achieve the opposite," said Peter von Maydell, senior currency strategist at UBS in London.
The dollar was quoted at 115.55 yen at 1530 gmt, down from late Thursday's European level of 116.25 but well off an intrasession low of 114.87.
Dollar/yen's sharp bounce from that level came amid market talk of Bank of England buying on behalf of the Bank of Japan, but there was no confirmation and traders were sceptical.

"Even if they do want dollar/yen lower, they'll be more than happy to see it settle around current levels for a while to at least give some semblance of stability, which is what the G7 communique was about after all," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist for Europe at Bank of America here.
The dollar was also dragged down against the mark ending at around 1.6942, having been around 1.7045.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
London's FTSE 100 ended up 12.7 points at 4,693.9.
The Paris CAC-40 index ended up 8.27 points at 2,784.28.
Frankfurt's DAX index ended up 42.44 points at 3,604.55.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar ended at 1.6942 marks and 115.55 yen compared with 1.6986 marks and 116.26 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold closed at $344.75 in London compared with London's close of $346.95 on Thursday. It slipped under $345 support after the New York opening, following silver lower. Silver ended at $4.71 down 15 cents after a sell-off in New York ended two near-static sessions.
